cards.a: A mechanism that breaks iBGP's full-mesh requirement by making one or more reflectors act as hubs that re-advertise iBGP-learned routes, cutting the session count from n(n-1)/2 to n. Reflection is controlled by three attributes, ORIGINATOR_ID, CLUSTER_LIST, and CLUSTER_ID, which guarantee loop-freedom when iBGP split horizon is bypassed.

cards.q: How much does a route reflector reduce iBGP sessions?
cards.a: From n(n-1)/2 sessions with a full mesh to n sessions per client, giving linear scaling. Full mesh collapses beyond about 10 routers while a reflector design scales linearly.

cards.q: What are the route reflector roles?
cards.a: RR re-advertises iBGP routes; a client is an iBGP peer of the RR that peers only with the RR; a non-client is an iBGP peer of the RR but is not a client. A client never peers with another client, the RR relays between them.

cards.q: What are the three rr reflection rules?
cards.a: A route learned from a client is sent to all other clients and non-clients; a route learned from a non-client is sent to clients only; a route learned from eBGP is sent to everyone. Otherwise iBGP-learned routes are not re-advertised (split horizon) except by these rules.

cards.q: What attributes prevent loops in route reflection?
cards.a: ORIGINATOR_ID carries the original router ID, and any router seeing its own ID drops the route; CLUSTER_ID identifies the reflector cluster; CLUSTER_LIST records the cluster IDs traversed, and any router in the list drops the route on re-receipt. Two RRs in one cluster share a CLUSTER_ID while distinct clusters have distinct IDs.

cards.q: How do you configure a route reflector?
cards.a: Under router bgp add neighbor 10.0.0.2 remote-as 65001 and neighbor 10.0.0.2 route-reflector-client per client, on the reflector. Clients keep normal iBGP config such as loopback and update-source and must peer with the reflector.

cards.q: How do you build a multi-cluster reflector design?
cards.a: Give each reflector its own cluster with bgp cluster-id 1, so several reflectors each with a unique cluster-id scale larger ASes; clients peer only with their local RR and the RRs peer with each other.

cards.q: Command to verify routes reflected through a cluster?
cards.a: show ip bgp cluster-list 1 shows routes carrying that cluster; show ip bgp neighbors <ip> and show ip bgp paths support the check.

cards.q: Where does a route learned from a non-client go?
cards.a: To clients only, not to other non-clients. The RR does not forward a non-client route to other non-clients.

cards.q: How does a route reflector safely bypass iBGP split horizon?
cards.a: It re-advertises iBGP-learned routes, but loop-freedom is guaranteed by ORIGINATOR_ID and CLUSTER_LIST instead of split horizon.
